evals.name: missing-top-level-permissions
evals.prompt: Harden the GitHub Actions workflow at fixtures/missing-permissions.yml. Apply the gha skill's enforcements and rewrite in place.
evals.expected_output: Workflow gains a top-level `permissions: contents: read` block inserted between `on:` and `jobs:`. The `actions/checkout@v4` ref is SHA-pinned with a `# v4.x.y` trailing comment and a preceding `# https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases` line.

assertions.name: top-level permissions block added
assertions.check: file contains a top-level `permissions:` key with `contents: read`

assertions.name: permissions placed between on: and jobs:
assertions.check: the `permissions:` block appears after the `on:` block and before the `jobs:` block

assertions.name: checkout action SHA-pinned
assertions.check: the `uses: actions/checkout@...` line ends in `@<40-hex>` not `@v4`

assertions.name: trailing tag comment present
assertions.check: the pinned `uses:` line has a `# v4.<...>` trailing comment matching a real release tag

assertions.name: releases-link comment above uses:
assertions.check: the line immediately above the pinned `uses:` is `# https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases` indented to match

evals.name: overbroad-workflow-write-scope
evals.prompt: Harden the GitHub Actions workflow at fixtures/overbroad-workflow-write.yml. Apply the gha skill's enforcements and rewrite in place.
evals.expected_output: Workflow-level `permissions:` tightened to `contents: read`. The `release` job gains its own `permissions:` block declaring BOTH `contents: write` AND `id-token: write` (full replacement per Rule A3) plus `contents: read` is not separately needed because `contents: write` implies read. The `test` job stays without a `permissions:` block (inherits the tightened workflow default).

assertions.name: workflow-level permissions narrowed
assertions.check: top-level `permissions:` no longer contains `contents: write` or `id-token: write`; instead contains `contents: read`

assertions.name: release job has explicit permissions block
assertions.check: the `release:` job declares its own `permissions:` block

assertions.name: release job permissions restates all needed scopes
assertions.check: release job's `permissions:` block contains `contents: write` AND `id-token: write` (A3: full replacement, not merge)

assertions.name: test job has no permissions block
assertions.check: the `test:` job has no `permissions:` block (inherits the tightened workflow default)

assertions.name: both checkout actions SHA-pinned
assertions.check: every `uses: actions/checkout@...` line ends in a 40-hex SHA, not `@v4`

evals.name: unpinned-uses-bulk-pin
evals.prompt: Harden the GitHub Actions workflow at fixtures/unpinned-uses.yml. Apply the gha skill's enforcements and rewrite in place.
evals.expected_output: All three `uses:` refs (`actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-go@v5`, `golangci/golangci-lint-action@v6`) are rewritten with a 40-char SHA + a `# vX.Y.Z` trailing comment + a preceding `# https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases` comment. The `contents: read` top-level permission is preserved unchanged (no edit needed).

assertions.name: actions/checkout pinned
assertions.check: the `actions/checkout` line uses `@<40-hex>` with a `# v4.<...>` comment

assertions.name: actions/setup-go pinned
assertions.check: the `actions/setup-go` line uses `@<40-hex>` with a `# v5.<...>` comment

assertions.name: golangci-lint-action pinned
assertions.check: the `golangci/golangci-lint-action` line uses `@<40-hex>` with a `# v6.<...>` comment

assertions.name: releases-link comment for every newly pinned action
assertions.check: each pinned `uses:` line has a `# https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases` line directly above it at matching indentation

assertions.name: tag comment is a concrete release tag, not floating major
assertions.check: trailing `# vX` comments are concrete (`# v4.2.0`), not the original floating major (`# v4`)

assertions.name: top-level permissions untouched
assertions.check: the existing `permissions: contents: read` block is preserved

evals.name: branch-ref-must-not-auto-pin
evals.prompt: Harden the GitHub Actions workflow at fixtures/branch-ref.yml. Apply the gha skill's enforcements and rewrite in place.
evals.expected_output: The `actions/checkout@v4` ref is SHA-pinned with the standard releases-link + trailing tag comment. The `some-org/some-action@main` ref is NOT rewritten — the skill reports the branch ref and asks the user whether to pin to HEAD SHA or a specific tag (Rule B3).

assertions.name: branch ref not auto-rewritten
assertions.check: the `some-org/some-action@main` line is still `@main` (or commented as 'needs user decision'), NOT silently rewritten to a SHA

assertions.name: branch ref flagged in report
assertions.check: the skill's report or response calls out `some-org/some-action@main` as a branch ref requiring user input

assertions.name: non-branch ref still gets pinned
assertions.check: the `actions/checkout@v4` line IS rewritten to `@<40-hex> # v4.<...>` with the releases-link comment above

evals.name: drift-comment-fix
evals.prompt: Harden the GitHub Actions workflow at fixtures/drift-comment.yml. Apply the gha skill's enforcements and rewrite in place. The SHA `11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683` is actions/checkout's v4.1.1 release, not v4.0.0 — verify and fix any drift.
evals.expected_output: The SHA is left unchanged. The trailing comment is rewritten from `# v4.0.0` to the actual tag(s) pointing at that SHA (e.g. `# v4.1.1`). The releases-link comment above is preserved unchanged.

assertions.name: SHA preserved
assertions.check: the SHA `11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683` is unchanged

assertions.name: trailing tag comment updated
assertions.check: the trailing comment is no longer `# v4.0.0`; it matches a real tag pointing at that SHA per `gh api repos/actions/checkout/tags`

assertions.name: releases-link comment preserved
assertions.check: the `# https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases` line directly above is still present and indented to match

assertions.name: no spurious second comment
assertions.check: there is exactly one trailing `# <tag>` comment on the `uses:` line (no duplication from the rewrite)
